narrative: Material PL1__M4811969 exhibits stable daily demand averaging 1,375 units with a mild upward trend (+1.1%) and normally-distributed residuals (CV=21.8%). Lead times are highly variable (CV=50.7%, range 0.44–5.97 days), driving a sigma_LTD of 1,660 units and a required safety stock of 2,731 units — 3.6x the current SAP setting of 755 units. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with ROP=5,883 and Q=10,904 (capacity-capped from EOQ of 12,905) is recommended, with 32.8 expected replenishments per year at a total annual inventory cost of ~$5,093.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock (755) is critically undersized; model recommends 2,731 (+262%) to achieve 95% service level.
Lead time CV=50.7% classified as UNSTABLE; supplier reliability improvement recommended.
Order quantity capped from EOQ 12,905 to 10,904 due to storage capacity constraint of 13,635 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is stable and continuous (all 216 working days show non-zero demand, CV=21.8%), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The high lead-time variability makes it critical to monitor inventory position continuously rather than periodically, to avoid stockouts between reviews.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (13,635 units) binds the order quantity, reducing it from 12,905 to 10,904. This increases order frequency by ~18% and raises annual ordering costs by ~$380, but remains feasible. If safety stock is increased to model recommendations, remaining storage drops to ~10,904 units, leaving minimal buffer for demand spikes.
